skill.name: gjalla-test-audit
skill.description: Audit test suites for false confidence from encoded bugs, duplicate coverage, excessive mocking, and tests that do not exercise production code.
skill.summary: Find weak, misleading, and redundant tests before they hide production regressions.
skill.author: gjalla

content.user_title: Audit Test Suites for False Confidence
content.value_statement: Weak tests can hide production bugs while inflating coverage metrics. This skill reviews test quality and identifies misleading, redundant, or excessively mocked tests.
actual_capabilities: Maps test directories, naming conventions, and test layers.
Compares tests with the production code they claim to exercise.
Identifies reimplemented logic, tautological mocks, and placeholder assertions.
Finds tests that encode incorrect behavior or use incompatible fixtures.
Classifies weak tests by deletion priority and replacement need.
Produces an impact report covering bugs, coverage gaps, and cleanup candidates.
limitations: Requires access to both test files and relevant production source files.
Does not prove that untested production behavior is correct.
Cleanup changes require explicit approval before files or test sections are removed.
Project-specific test frameworks may require additional interpretation.

use_cases.title: Review a legacy test suite
use_cases.description: Find tests that inflate confidence without protecting current production behavior.

use_cases.title: Harden a risky subsystem
use_cases.description: Compare critical source paths with tests and identify missing realistic coverage.

use_cases.title: Improve quality governance
use_cases.description: Classify weak tests and create a prioritized remediation report for the team.

prompt_templates.title: Basic test quality review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the test suite in [directory]. Identify placeholder tests, tests without source imports, and obvious duplicated coverage. Report findings without changing files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an initial review of a small project.

prompt_templates.title: Mocking quality audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review tests for [component]. Compare each test with its source code. Flag tautological mocks and explain which production defects each test cannot detect.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when mocked tests dominate a subsystem.

prompt_templates.title: Critical path coverage audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit tests covering [critical path]. Rank gaps by production impact, identify encoded bugs, and recommend realistic integration or round-trip tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before changing security, billing, or data access behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Full remediation plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [test scope] across all test layers. Classify findings into deletion and replacement tiers. Estimate coverage impact and propose approved cleanup waves.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a comprehensive suite modernization plan.

output_examples.input: Audit the account service tests for tautological database mocks.
output_examples.output: Tier 2 finding: three tests return hardcoded database rows and assert those same values. Replace them with database-backed behavior tests.

output_examples.input: Find tests that do not exercise production code.
output: Tier 1: The test recreates the source decision logic locally.
Evidence: The test imports no production module.
Action: Remove the duplicate logic test after approval and add a source-level test.

output_examples.input: Review overlapping unit and integration tests.
output_examples.output: Tier 3 finding: the mocked unit test duplicates the stronger database-backed scenario. Keep unique edge cases and remove redundant coverage after approval.

best_practices: Provide the relevant test files and production source files together.
Prioritize security boundaries, data access, and core business logic.
Run tests and coverage between approved cleanup waves.
anti_patterns: Do not judge test quality from coverage percentages alone.
Do not remove weak tests before identifying replacement coverage.
Do not classify mocked tests without comparing their behavior to production code.

faq.question: Does this skill modify tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings first and requires approval before cleanup changes.

faq.question: Which test frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The process is framework independent, with specific examples for Vitest, PGlite, SQLite, and common mocking patterns.

faq.question: Can it detect tests that encode production bugs?
faq.answer: It compares assertions, fixtures, and source behavior to identify inconsistencies that may preserve incorrect behavior.

faq.question: Does it replace code coverage tools?
faq.answer: No. It interprets test quality and uses coverage results as supporting evidence.

faq.question: What source access does the audit require?
faq.answer: It needs the selected tests, related production code, and enough project structure to identify test layers.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Findings are ranked by production impact, test realism, duplicated coverage, and the need for replacement tests.
